Subject: Post-call: Exec recap & procurement path - NexAvante

Hi Sonia / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our exec-level discussion so we have alignment for next steps. Happy to jump on a short follow-up with procurement if helpful.

Key business outcomes you called out
- Reduce customer support cost for claims triage by ~40% via faster first-touch classification and suggested response templates.
- Improve processing throughput during month-end spikes (current peaks are ~3x baseline).
- Reduce latency of downstream routing to specialists (goal: sub-500ms per request for prioritization).

Primary pain points
- Current pipeline is brittle: legacy pre-processing makes inference slow and inconsistent.
- High cost per API call with current third-party vendor and limited ability to tune quantization/performance.
- Governance: need SOC 2 evidence, KMS for customer keys, and a clear data residency approach for EU/US customers.

Technical & procurement constraints
- Must support KMS-backed encryption for customer-specific keys (NexAvante uses AWS KMS).
- On-premise option is on the table for regulated clients but initial rollout should be hosted/dedicated.
- Procurement prefers a 12-month committed capacity contract with a 60-day implementation SLA.

Risks we flagged
- Data transformation work may add ~4-6 weeks depending on schema heterogeneity.
- If we must do on-prem, timeline and costs increase materially.

Proposed next steps
1) Marissa: share SOC 2 report + draft SOW + ballpark quote (attached). (Today)
2) NexAvante: share procurement contact + preferred PO cadence and any vendor security questionnaire. (This week)
3) Technical working session with Aditya to scope data transformation and pilot success metrics (propose 60-90 minute session). (Next week)
4) If procurement is happy, draft agreement and target a pilot start by early August (tentative).

If I've missed anything or you want different prioritization, let me know.

Thanks, looking forward to partnering.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Marissa,

Appreciate the clear recap. High level: this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from my side before we loop procurement formally:

1) Data residency / KMS: For EU customers we need proof we can segregate keys and guarantee EU-only processing. Can you confirm Redwood's approach here and timeline to enable?
2) SOC 2: please send the latest SOC 2 Type II report (or an attestation) so our security team can start the review.
3) Ballpark pricing: procurement will need a ballpark number for a 12-month committed plan for ~10M tokens/month baseline with 3x spike allowance. A single-line estimate is fine for now.
4) Pilot success metrics: we like the 60-90 min working session idea, please propose 2 slots next week.

Tom (CC) is our procurement lead, Tom, can you share your standard SOW/PO template and preferred escalation path?

Hi Sonia / Marissa / Tom,

Thanks for the notes. A few technical clarifications and recommendations from the SE side:

- KMS/data residency: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for encryption-at-rest for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted, we can provide envelope encryption and integrate with customer KMS (AWS) so keys never leave AWS regions you control. To guarantee EU-only processing we can pin requests to EU capacity and provide an auditable routing policy (policy + audit logs). Timeline: we can enable region-pinning and KMS integration in our onboarding plan; estimate 2-3 weeks of config work and an ops review.

- Pilot scope & data transformation: your schema variability (as discussed) is the key unknown. Typical path: ingest sample batch (2-10k records), run a transformation script (we can pair on this), and run the pilot for a 2-4 week window to validate latency and quality. If you want, we'll prepare a short checklist for the pilot data requirements.

- Pricing ballpark: attaching the initial quote. Rough estimate for planning: $28k-$42k/month on committed capacity for the baseline + negotiated overage/spike buffer. Final terms depend on model selection and quantization profile.

I've attached: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2025.pdf, NXV-Draft-SOW-Redwood.docx, NXV-Initial-Quote-Redwood.xlsx.

Proposed working session slots (PST):
- Tue, Jun 23 10:00-11:30
- Wed, Jun 24 14:00-15:30

Happy to present a short 30-min technical readout + 30-min hands-on if you'd like.

Thanks,
